Russia launches massive drone and missile barrage across Ukraine

By ILLIA NOVIKOV and HANNA ARHIROVA Updated 4:12 AM EST

KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Russia launched one of its largest aerial assaults of the war against Ukraine, firing scores of drones and missiles that killed at least four people and knocked out power to hundreds of thousands, Ukrainian officials said.

The barrage targeted energy infrastructure in the Zaporizhzhia region and the capital, Kyiv, as Moscow intensified its campaign against Ukraine's power grid heading into the coldest months of winter.

Rescue workers pulled survivors from a collapsed apartment block in the eastern city, where a drone struck a residential building overnight. Emergency services said the search for people trapped under the rubble continued through the morning.

"This was a deliberate attack on civilian infrastructure," said regional governor Ivan Rocheleau, adding that repair crews were working to restore heat and electricity before nightfall.

Ukraine's air force said it shot down the majority of the incoming drones but that a number of ballistic missiles penetrated air defenses, causing the deadly strikes in Zaporizhzhia and surrounding towns.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned the barrage and renewed his appeal to Western allies for additional air-defense systems, warning that Ukraine's grid could not withstand a sustained winter campaign without them.

The strikes came as Russia pressed a grinding ground offensive in the east, where its forces have made incremental gains at heavy cost over recent weeks. Analysts said the aerial campaign was designed to sap Ukrainian morale and stretch its limited air defenses.

Kyiv residents sheltered in metro stations as air-raid sirens sounded across the capital for several hours. Power was later restored to most districts, though officials cautioned that rolling blackouts would continue while engineers assessed the damage.
